subject: Retention window exception — post-demo recap & next steps
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@teletriage.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@teletriage.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — retention question

Thanks for the demo today, Ben — appreciate the walkthrough. A couple quick clarifications from our privacy team:

- TeleTriage handles clinical intake forms; some prompts contain patient identifiers (name, phone, MRN).
- Our legal team is pushing for a 0-retention option for PII (or at least a sub-24 hour window) while we pilot.
- We also need clarity on where KV/cache remnants might land (are any aggregates stored outside the customer VPC for hosted mode?).

Can Redwood support a short-term pilot where session-level inputs are dropped after processing (0-retention) and only anonymized telemetry is kept for 30 days? If not fully 0-retention, what are the minimal audit artifacts you would still retain and how are they protected?

Appreciate a short summary + recommended path and any evidence (SOC2/audit logs) we can pass to legal.

—Sarah
Head of Product, TeleTriage

(attachment: teletriage-dpa-draft.docx)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@teletriage.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — retention question

Sarah — thanks, great questions. Quick recap and options we discussed on the call: 

1) Hosted API (fastest): default behavior stores KV/cache for session reuse and telemetry for 90 days; we can offer a short-term configuration to aggressively expire session inputs after 0–6 hours for the pilot, but truly "never stored" requires using Private deployment or a routed proxy that strips PII before hitting Redwood.

2) Dedicated/Private: with Private (VPC) we can support 0-retention for model inputs — inputs can be configured to be processed in-memory only and not written to persistent logs. We will need a short engineering change to the default routing to enable in-memory-only mode for your workspace.

3) Minimal artifacts: even with 0-retention, we currently retain service-level traces (request ids, timestamp, routing metadata) for 30 days to support debugging and SLA investigation — these do not contain user text by default and can be pseudonymized.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll loop in Neha (privacy/compliance) and Steph (solutions) to outline a pilot runbook and required ops changes.
- Neha will provide SOC2 evidence and our standard audit-log schema.
- If TeleTriage signs a short DPA amendment we can spin up a 30-day private pilot with in-memory processing.

Would you prefer we start with a hosted short-window (same infra, fast) or go straight to a private pilot? I can put timelines together either way.

Cheers,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-data-retention-matrix.pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Demo follow-up — retention question

Folks — forwarding TeleTriage ask (see below). They want a 0-retention pilot or at least a <24h window for PII. Legal asked for evidence/SOC2 and a clear list of what artifacts we would still keep.

Key constraints:
- They will start as hosted but want assurance we can do in-memory-only once procurement signs.
- Procurement also asked for a short DPA amendment and a simple runbook.

Can we scope a minimal runbook and a toggle plan for a 30-day pilot that:
A) ensures session inputs are not persisted to disk,
B) confirms KV cache destruction policy and timeline,
C) provides an audit log extract format that contains no raw text fields (only request ids, timestamps, and hashed ids).

I put a tentative timeline below:
- Today: Neha to confirm what evidence (SOC2 sections, logging screenshots) we can provide.
- 10/2: Steph to give an ops-level checklist and rough eng effort (hrs).
- 10/4: proposal + DPA patch to TeleTriage.

Appreciate a short reply with bullets — Sarah is waiting for an internal review tomorrow.

On Sep 30, 2026, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@teletriage.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the demo today, Ben — appreciate the walkthrough. A couple quick clarifications from our privacy team:...

—Ben

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Demo follow-up — retention question

Ben / team — here's a concise plan we can share with TeleTriage tomorrow. I kept it short so legal can paste into procurement.

1) Pilot modes (choose one):
   - Hosted short-window: configure workspace TTL = 6 hours for session inputs; KV cache cleared every 6 hours; telemetry pseudonymized. Low engineering lift (config change + Ops ticket).
   - Private (VPC) in-memory: inputs processed in-memory only, no persistent logs; requires enabling in-memory flag and a quick infra validation (approx 1–2 sprints of infra eng for hardened automation).

2) What we will always retain (audit-friendly):
   - Request id, timestamp, model variant, region, route (no raw text).
   - If requested, hashes of input ids (sha256) for correlating events without revealing content.

3) Evidence pack (attached):
   - SOC2 summary + scope sections (we can redact customer-identifying examples).
   - Audit-log schema (CSV sample) showing no free-text columns.
   - Runbook checklist for enabling the pilot + rollback plan.

4) Proposed DPA amendment language (short):
   - Add clause: "Customer may request in-memory processing for specified workspaces for the purpose of a time‑boxed pilot; Redwood will not persist raw customer-supplied request content to disk for the duration of the pilot."

Next steps:
- Steph: please confirm engineering hours and any risks you see (esp. cache poisoning or functional regressions).
- Marissa: can you own the DPA patch and forward to TeleTriage procurement with the evidence pack?

I attached the retention matrix and a sample redlined DPA. If TeleTriage wants 0-retention as a permanent prod setting we'll need a security review and an ops runbook. For the pilot we can move fast.

—Neha Kapoor
Manager, Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
(attachments: redwood-data-retention-matrix.pdf, teletriage-dpa-draft.docx)
